storyBlocks.sourceHtml: Vanessa had made it through breast cancer after rounds of chemotherapy and radiation. By the time we bought the property, she was done with treatment, but that does not mean life had simply snapped back to normal. We were both still shaken. Still stressed. Still carrying around the heaviness that comes after something like that. Cancer is not subtle. It is not poetic. It is hard, direct, exhausting, and life-changing. And after all of it, we knew we needed something quieter and more peaceful.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: I found the property online sometime around April of 2022, and I felt like I needed to go see it immediately. Something about it grabbed me before I could explain why.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: When we pulled in with our realtor, it was a mess.
storyBlocks.text: When we pulled in with our realtor, it was a mess.
storyBlocks.html: When we pulled in with our realtor, it was a mess.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: There was junk everywhere. Old broke-down cars. Trailers. An RV or something sitting there. The whole place looked like it had been abandoned in stages. As we walked the property, we kept finding half-finished projects and rough little setups that looked like somebody had started building a dream and then stopped somewhere in the middle.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: Vanessa thought I was crazy.

storyBlocks.html: Vanessa thought I was crazy.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: And honestly, she had good reason.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: But I have always been the kind of person who can see the forest through the trees. Under all the junk, under the unfinished work, under the strange layout and the rough edges, I could feel something peaceful there. The place had a calming feeling to it, even in the shape it was in. I could see what it might become.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: That same day, we put in an offer.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: We offered a little less than asking, and we added a condition that the junk had to be removed or the sellers would lose a retainer. We were serious about the place, but we were not trying to buy the mess with it.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: Even after the offer was accepted, it was not smooth sailing.

storyBlocks.sourceHtml: Getting the loan closed turned into its own ordeal. The property did not have a furnace with a thermostat, and because of that, we kept running into problems finding insurance. That was one of those things we had never really thought about before, how strange and picky insurance companies can be about the smallest details. We searched around, made calls, worked with the credit union that was handling the loan, and kept pushing forward until we finally found a company willing to insure the property.
